name: Sonata Software Ltd
title: Sonata Software Ltd - 532221 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: International EBITDA fell to 15.4% from 20.2% and utilisation dropped to 88.5% from 91.8% on a delayed large-deal ramp; management says ramp is "largely behind us" but gave no numbers, and no capacity signal is given.

summary.headline: Sonata Q1 FY27 consolidated PAT fell 17.1% QoQ to Rs108.6 crore on Rs35.4 crore forex hit; international EBITDA dropped to 15.4% from 20.2%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 29.3% QoQ to Rs3,279.1 crore, but the domestic jump reflects the call's own framing and is not explained in detail. International services revenue was flat QoQ in constant currency at $82 million, with EBITDA margin down to 15.4% from 20.2% on a one-time compensation benefit in Q4, utilisation dip from a delayed large-deal ramp-up, forex (about 50 bps) and AI investments. Utilisation fell to 88.5% from 91.8%, and management said the large-deal ramp-up completes in Q2 FY27. Management focused on an AI-native engineering strategy, a 1.18x book-to-bill and a rising AI order book, but gave no quantitative margin guidance.

segments.name: International services
segments.commentary: Revenue $82 million, flat QoQ in constant currency; EBITDA margin 15.4% vs 20.2% in Q4 FY26. Headcount 6,293 (vs 6,283), attrition 13%, offshore mix 70% (vs 68%).

segments.name: Domestic business
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs2,505.6 crore and gross contribution Rs78.5 crore (+14.5% YoY). Management said some customers at risk of OEM direct billing have renewed through Sonata; SMC and corporate software business grew about 82% YoY.

guidance_outlook: Management expects EBITDA to show positive traction every quarter in FY27, with some one-time items normalising in coming quarters.
Large-deal ramp-up expected to complete in Q2 FY27; management said margin trajectory should turn positive from next quarter.
Management declined to give a steady-state international EBITDA margin, saying it would not be guidance.
Tax rate (ETR) is about 25 percent normally; Q1 benefited from an exceptional US R&D tax credit.
Management expects domestic financial performance to keep improving in Q2 and the rest of FY27 and said domestic growth momentum will be maintained.
capex_capacity: Forward deployed engineer pool to be expanded to about 100 people by August 2026.
Sonata University has trained 93% of the workforce in AI.
Workbench, an agentic AI service delivery platform under Harmoni.ai, launched in the quarter.
Investments in AI advisory and FDE talent are expected to continue for a couple of quarters before paying back.
demand_pricing: Seven customers added in Q1 FY27, consistent with the prior two quarters; top 10 clients were 51% of revenue, shift attributed to the 11-20 client bucket growing faster.
Clients above $5 million run rate: 12 (flat QoQ); clients at $3-5 million: nine (flat QoQ); management said clients above $1 million are moving up buckets rather than being lost.
Management said 21% of engagements are output-based.
Management said top five clients show stability, with growth expected to return in a few quarters.
Domestic: partner network broadened across all hyperscalers and into non-hyperscaler OEM tools, with an AI tools and platforms push with OEM partners.
Microsoft invited Sonata to the Copilot agents and platform engineering Depth Partner Program; management said the programme launched only about two to three weeks earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Is the domestic business sustainably back to double-digit gross contribution growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is confident growth momentum will continue and that the earlier OEM-related issues have been overcome.

qa_highlights.question: Why did top-10 client revenue fall 6% QoQ, and is pricing or productivity pass-through the cause?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the share change to 11-20 clients growing well and new wins landing in that group; it denied discounts or productivity pass-through. It declined to disclose absolute top-10 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for TMT and retail/manufacturing, which also declined?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the BFSI share grew faster than expected, which lowered the R&D share, and that TMT growth will come from hyperscalers and enterprise and packaged-software clients.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the margin drop and the timing of recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the margin drop came from a large-deal ramp delay, billing and paperwork delays, one-time items, forex and AI investments; it expects a positive margin trajectory from next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did net cash fall QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it reflected vendor payouts linked to domestic turnover; net cash was ~Rs65 crore vs ~Rs30 crore, and gross cash was ~Rs565 crore vs ~Rs605 crore; no one-time payment.

qa_highlights.question: What were the Q1 international deal wins and ticket sizes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about seven customers were won, including a three-year, multimillion-dollar modernisation and managed-services deal; the others have growth potential.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state international margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a range, saying it expects a positive direction in coming quarters. On the domestic large deal, margin is measured in absolute gross contribution, which is positive and accretive.

risks_watch: International EBITDA margin (15.4%) needs to recover as the large-deal ramp completes in Q2 FY27; utilisation at 88.5%.
Forex volatility: about Rs28 crore PAT impact in Q1 by management's count, Rs35.4 crore in the consolidated figure.
Revenue concentration: top-10 share 51% with absolute top-10 revenue no longer disclosed; top-five growth still not back.
Domestic business: OEM direct-billing risk persists, and DSO rose to 65 days from 47 days.
Net cash fell QoQ to ~Rs565 crore gross; vendor payouts are tied to domestic turnover.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the AI strategy and medium-term growth, but cautious on near-term margin and revenue: management repeatedly called the drag one-time and gave no quantitative margin guidance. On client-level questions (top 10 revenue, cash decline, deal ticket size) answers were brief and partly deflected.
key_quotes: Base utilization continues to operate at 88.5% as we encountered a delay in a large deal ramp-up and AI capability incubation, which caused a slight reduction in the utilization.
From this quarter, we expect EBITDA to have a positive traction every quarter in this year further.

I am not able to define a stable state EBITDA margin I do not want that will become a guidance kind of a nature, but definitely it will move towards a positive direction for us in the coming quarters.

adds.what: Forward deployed engineer pool expanded to about 100 people (people, not productive plant capacity)

growth.why: No quantitative revenue guidance; management expects domestic momentum and EBITDA traction each quarter, backed by a 1.18x book-to-bill, a $97.4M order book, a $21.4M AI order book and the large-deal ramp completing in Q2 FY27, though the brief gives no hard numbers on delivery.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: International EBITDA margin fell to 15.4% from 20.2% in Q4 FY26, management says the large-deal ramp completes in Q2 FY27 and margin trajectory turns positive from next quarter, though it gave no quantitative steady-state margin.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Forward deployed engineer pool to grow to about 100 people by August 2026, but this is headcount rather than productive plant capacity; international utilisation is 88.5%, so no hard capacity addition is disclosed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: International USD revenue was flat at $82M QoQ in constant currency, but the 1.18x book-to-bill, $97.4M order book and $21.4M AI order book point to modest recovery; management expects top-five client growth back in a few quarters.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 88.5%, which is high, but the company is an IT services firm and the call discussed people-based investment (FDE pool, AI talent) rather than a new facility; no capex plan was disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no quantitative revenue or margin guidance and declined to give a steady-state international margin, so there is no basis for an upgrade in the window.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Margin recovery depends on the large-deal ramp completing in Q2 FY27 and on utilisation recovering from 88.5% (vs 91.8%); forex and AI investment costs persist for a couple of quarters.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Workbench agentic AI platform under Harmoni.ai launched this quarter, and Microsoft Copilot agents programme invite just started, with the AI-led pipeline at $340M (+21%).

rows.label: AI order book growth
rows.why: AI order book rose to $21.4M (18.2% of order book) from $16.9M in Q4 FY26, a 27% increase, against a $340M AI-led pipeline up 21%.

rows.label: One-time items normalise
rows.why: Management says one-time items, including the Q4 compensation benefit reversal, will normalise in coming quarters, with EBITDA showing positive traction each quarter in FY27.

rows.label: Domestic DSO normalisation
rows.why: Domestic DSO rose to 65 days from 47 days; management called it seasonal, but the brief gives no normalisation target, and the net cash fell to ~Rs65 crore from ~Rs30 crore on vendor payouts.
